# Corrugated Die-Room Tooling Coordinator Rekey

## Problem statement

Corrugated-box and packaging plants keep a "die room" that stages, inspects, and
repairs the steel-rule cutting dies and print plates used on their die-cutters and
flexo presses — a support function adjacent to tool-and-die making. A dedicated
"Tooling Coordinator" role exists at multiple plants and companies specifically to
run this intake: inspect each die/plate as it comes off a job, tag it, log it (by
tool number) on a die/tooling spreadsheet, and separately scan and key the
associated print-card and CAD identifiers "into the system" so production can find
the right tooling for the next scheduled job. This is described as a recurring,
full-time, hourly position — not a side duty — at more than one employer, which
implies real ongoing labor cost, not a one-time setup task.

## Evidence

- [type: job-posting] (2026-09-09, live) Pratt Industries, Rock Hill, SC —
  "Tooling Coordinator." Duties include "Assign and log tooling numbers for easy
  tracking," "Maintain accurate records of tooling assignments and updates," and
  "assist with scanning and documenting print cards and CADs in the system," plus
  physically inspecting and staging cutting dies and print plates.
  https://careers.prattindustries.com/en/jobs/0138-24023/tooling-coordinator/
- [type: job-posting] (2026-09-11, live) Pratt Industries, Fort Worth, TX (3rd
  shift) — "Tooling Coordinator." Duties include "Maintain die spreadsheets and
  track inventory," "Assign and log tooling numbers for easy tracking," and
  document print cards and CAD files "in the system," across multiple storage
  locations.
  https://careers.prattindustries.com/en/jobs/108-24226/tooling-coordinator/
- [type: job-posting] (retrieved 2026-09-15, undated, since expired) Pratt
  Industries, La Vergne, TN — "Tooling Coordinator." Describes keeping "die
  spread sheets," checking in incoming print plates, assigning IDs "from the
  Print or Cutting Die Log Book," and entering that information "into HRMS."
  https://www.simplyhired.com/job/h7KZSqAxMP_pTfjl2cE_Uwu-69kNIeLtadrxX6_NW0_C9wncefuPWQ
- [type: job-posting] (retrieved 2026-09-15, snippet only, full posting blocked
  by bot-protection) Hood Container Corporation, Sandston, VA — "Tooling
  Coordinator" listing described as "Managing tooling asset lifecycle in
  corrugated packaging manufacturing," confirming the same role exists at a
  second employer, not just Pratt Industries.
  https://www.simplyhired.com/job/u4c864-SU3MK-BcMAHG7ywyg-2HlRO8S8fBB3zR0eVhxfk3X9R99zQ

## Automation hypothesis

SPECULATIVE. If the die/print-plate log (paper log book or spreadsheet) and the
plant's production/ERP system where print-card and CAD identifiers are scanned in
are genuinely disconnected, a lightweight intake app — barcode/QR-tag each die or
plate at first inspection, capture condition and location on a phone or tablet,
and push that record directly into the plant's production system via API or a
scheduled export — could collapse the "log on paper, then re-key into HRMS/ERP"
two-step into one. This is tractable only if the target production system
(unnamed in these postings — likely an ERP or MES module) exposes an import path;
if it is a closed legacy system with no integration surface, this stays a
spreadsheet-replacement product at best. Worth confirming which ERP/MES corrugated
plants commonly run before assuming an integration exists.
retired_language_body:
# Foreign-Language Study-Abroad Syllabus Equivalency Review

## Problem statement

When a student takes a language or literature course abroad that is not already
in a university's pre-approved articulation table, responsibility for deciding
whether it satisfies a home-institution requirement falls to the language
department itself — typically the department chair or a designated faculty
member — rather than to the registrar's transfer-credit system. The reviewer
receives a syllabus (sometimes in the target language), compares its content
and level by hand to home course offerings, and returns a decision on a
department-specific paper or PDF form. The registrar only updates the official
transcript after the host institution's transcript separately arrives, "which
may be months after the student's return" in at least one documented case.
This is recurring, per-student, per-course manual document comparison with no
integration between the study-abroad office's intake, the department's
subject-matter review, and the registrar's degree-audit system.

## Evidence

- [type: job-posting] (2026-08-17) University of Wyoming, "Coordinator,
  Transfer Articulation – Transfer Relations": the role "coordinates with
  academic departments, Registrar, Admissions, and external partners... to
  support articulation updates, resolve discrepancies, and ensure shared
  understanding of transfer equivalencies," and separately "ensures
  consistency of articulation data across Banner, published catalog, website,
  and internal/external transfer tools" — i.e., the same equivalency decision
  has to be manually re-entered/reconciled across at least four separate
  records once a department (such as a language department) renders it.
  https://jobs.chronicle.com/job/38026968/coordinator-transfer-articulation-transfer-relations/

- [type: job-posting] (2026-08-24) Virginia Tech, "Assistant Registrar for
  Transfer Credit" ($65,000–$70,000): responsible for "overseeing the
  evaluation of transfer credit" and "collaborating with academic departments
  to facilitate the seamless integration of transfer coursework," requiring
  "knowledge of transfer credit evaluation, course equivalencies, and academic
  policy interpretation" — a dedicated salaried role built around routing
  course-level decisions to departments and reconciling the result back into
  student records.
  https://jobs.chronicle.com/job/38029726/assistant-registrar-for-transfer-credit/

- [type: institutional] (page live as of 2026-09, references terms through
  2027) Pace University, Modern Languages and Cultures study-abroad guidance:
  "Department Chairs – have the sole authority to identify a Pace equivalent
  course for a foreign course taken abroad." A course not already in Pace's
  pre-approved list requires the student to submit a "Not Previously Approved
  Course Equivalency Form" that includes the foreign course syllabus for the
  chair to evaluate against Pace's own catalog by hand, with fixed submission
  deadlines (e.g., "no later than March 1" for summer programs).
  https://www.pace.edu/study-abroad/getting-started/course-credit-while-studying-abroad
  [Note: "institutional" is a source-type tag outside the skill's defined
  vocabulary — this is the university's own self-published operating
  procedure, not a job posting, forum post, or regulatory filing. Flagging
  explicitly rather than mislabeling it into an existing tier.]

- [type: institutional] (page live as of 2026-09) University of Miami,
  Department of Modern Languages and Literatures: students obtain a "course
  equivalency form" directly from the department office (with a specific room
  number given) for each course; "Upon receipt of the host institution
  transcript by the Office of Study Abroad, which may be months after the
  student's return, the course titles and grades will be added to the UM
  official transcript" — documenting both the manual per-course department
  sign-off and the multi-month lag before it reaches the academic record.
  https://mll.as.miami.edu/undergraduate/study-abroad/index.html

- [type: institutional] (page live as of 2026-09, references Spring 2026
  major-declaration deadlines) Tulane University, Department of Communication
  study-abroad course-approval guidance: "If the course is not taught in
  English, students can submit the syllabus in the original language," to be
  evaluated personally by the department's Director of Undergraduate Studies
  by email, accepted only as a full syllabus in Word or PDF format — showing
  a named individual faculty member acting as the sole manual reviewer of
  untranslated foreign documents, with no shared tooling with the registrar
  or study-abroad office.
  https://liberalarts.tulane.edu/communication/academics/study-abroad

## Automation hypothesis

SPECULATIVE. A tool that let a department reviewer upload or forward a
foreign-institution syllabus (including non-English text) and get a structured
side-by-side comparison against the home catalog's course descriptions and
learning outcomes — using translation plus retrieval against the institution's
own catalog data — could compress the manual read-and-compare step and produce
a structured equivalency record the registrar could ingest directly, instead
of a decision that lives only on a department-specific PDF form until a
transcript arrives months later. This would require buy-in from the
department (the actual decision-maker, per Pace's "sole authority" language)
and an integration surface into whatever transfer-articulation module the
registrar's SIS uses (e.g., Banner, as referenced in the Wyoming posting);
neither is confirmed to be tractable from public sources, and the market here
is one department-level buyer at a time unless sold through a study-abroad or
registrar's-office platform instead.
